sources.locator: Chapter 9 (Poincare Duality, Intersection theory, and Linking numbers) Sections 9.1-9.3, printed pp. 249-263 (PDF pp. 260-274), together with Chapter 8 (Tubular Neighborhoods, more on Transversality, and Intersection Theory).
sources.reading_verification: The design register's URL bookR3.pdf returns 404; the same book was recovered live from the author's current Stanford link bookR4.pdf (5,961,518 bytes, 6,879 PDF pages of extracted text layer) and the text layer was extracted and read for Chapter 9 Sections 1-3. Read at the statement level: Definition 9.1 (shriek/umkehr maps), Definition 9.2 and Theorem 9.2 (Thom collapse and the Thom isomorphism in cohomology), Corollary 9.3 (collapse pullback of the Thom class is the Poincare dual), Definition 9.3 and Theorems 9.4-9.5 (the intersection product is represented by transverse intersections), Theorem 9.7 (the de Rham interpretation), Theorem 9.9 and Corollaries 9.10-9.11 (self-intersection and the Euler class; nowhere-zero sections), Theorems 9.12-9.13 (Euler characteristic and the diagonal expansion), and the representability remark after Theorem 9.5. The proofs of Theorems 9.2/9.4/9.9 were read; they use the homology Thom isomorphism and leave one normalization sign to the reader, which is why this page proves the dual-of-a-submanifold statement locally (item lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold) rather than citing the draft.

contents.name: Definition 9.1 and the shriek/umkehr construction
contents.support: The umkehr map is computed inside the theorem's proof through cap and the duality isomorphisms; no separate item is minted for it.

contents.name: Definition 9.2, Theorem 9.2 and Corollary 9.3: Thom collapse, the Thom isomorphism in cohomology, and c^*u = PD of the submanifold
contents.support: This is exactly the dual-of-a-submanifold statement; DT-12 proves its tubular-neighbourhood form from the AT Thom interfaces because DT-16 owns the collapse form on a later page.

contents.name: Definition 9.3 and Theorems 9.4-9.5: the intersection product is Poincare dual to the cup product and is represented by transverse intersections
contents.support: The central AT interface; the sign of the ordered factors is fixed at build time by the library cap/cup conventions.

contents.name: Theorem 9.7: de Rham interpretation of the intersection number by Thom forms
contents.reason: The differential-form interpretation of the intersection pairing is a de Rham-theoretic refinement owned by the de Rham degree pair; this page states and proves the singular-cohomology identity only, so no de Rham machinery is minted here.

contents.name: Theorem 9.9 and Corollaries 9.10-9.11: self-intersection of the zero section, the Euler class, and nowhere-zero sections
contents.support: Proved through the zero-locus duality and the signed zero count.

contents.name: Theorem 9.12: evaluation of the Euler class is the Euler characteristic
contents.reason: The Euler-characteristic identification needs the vector-field index and Poincare-Hopf machinery of the later Euler/index pair; this page stops at the evaluation of e(TM) on [M] in the diagonal corollary.

contents.name: Theorem 9.13 and the diagonal Thom-class expansion
contents.reason: The Kunneth expansion of the diagonal class and the alternating trace formula are owned by the Lefschetz pair, which consumes this page's diagonal self-intersection corollary.

contents.name: Remark after Theorem 9.5: not every integral homology class is represented by a manifold
contents.support: Recorded verbatim as the representability caveat of the geometric model.

contents.name: Exercise 1 after Corollary 9.6: RP^1 in RP^2 cannot be moved off itself (mod two self-intersection one)
contents.support: The Mobius/projective-line counterexample with nonorientable normal bundle.

contents.name: Sections 8.1-8.2: tubular neighbourhoods, transversality and intersection-theoretic setup
contents.support: Only the smooth tubular and transverse-intersection interfaces are used, and those are supplied by the earlier DG pages; no Cohen-specific construction is imported.

sources.locator: Ch. 2 Section 4, printed pp. 79-80 (Mobius band and RP^1 in RP^2, mod two); Ch. 3 Section 3, printed pp. 107-118 (oriented intersection numbers, local signs, factor order, the diagonal and I(Delta,Delta)).
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 236-page PDF (3,472,576 bytes) and inspected the text layer on printed pp. 79-80 and 107-118 with the running heads identifying the printed pagination; the Ch. 2 section-4 example of the Mobius central curve and the Ch. 3 section-3 orientation-number definitions and exercises were read against the displayed formulas.

contents.name: Ch. 2 Section 4, pp. 79-80: the Mobius band central circle has mod two self-intersection 1 and RP^1 in RP^2 cannot be pushed off itself
contents.support: The mod two survival with a nonorientable normal line.

contents.name: Ch. 3 Section 3, pp. 107-108: the local orientation number and the definition of I(f,Z)
contents.support: Reused only through the already-published DT-11 local sign and intersection-number items; the identity with the cup pairing is not in GP and is proved here.

contents.name: Ch. 3 Section 3, p. 112: the submanifold case and the ordered factor convention
contents.support: The first-factor-first order is the published DT-11 convention.

contents.name: Ch. 3 Section 3, p. 115: I(f,g)=(-1)^{(dim X)(dim Z)}I(g,f)
contents.support: The library's published theorem is the consumed form; no new sign convention is minted.

contents.name: Ch. 3 Section 3, exercises: I(Delta,Delta)=chi(M) and the diagonal/self-intersection computations
contents.reason: The identification of the diagonal self-intersection with the Euler characteristic needs the index and Poincare-Hopf machinery of the later Euler/index pair; this page proves only Delta.Delta = evaluation of e(TM).

sources.title: Eleny-Nicoleta Ionel (notes by Andrew Lin), Stanford Math 215B Differential Topology, Winter 2023 (complete 63-page lecture notes)
sources.locator: Lectures 14-16, printed pp. 43-52: the Thom class and isomorphism, the intersection product dual to the cup product, Theorems 138-139, Corollary 143, Theorem 144 and Corollary 146.
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 63-page PDF (543,433 bytes) and read Lectures 14-16 in the extracted text layer: Definition 135 and Fact 136 (Euler class, naturality, nowhere-zero sections), Theorem 138 (informal) and Theorem 139 with its proof sketch (the Poincare dual of a submanifold is the normal Thom class, via the collapse and compact-support duality), Corollary 143 (degree as a local signed sum), Theorem 144 (self-intersection is the Euler class of the normal bundle; the Euler class is dual to the zero locus of a generic section) and its proof through the Thom-isomorphism diagram, and Examples 145-146. The one step left as 'we won't do that' (the commutative-square verification) is exactly the local generator computation carried out here in lem-normal-thom-class-realizes-the-poincare-dual-of-a-submanifold.

contents.name: Definition 135 and Fact 136: the Euler class as the zero-section pullback of the Thom class, its naturality, products and nowhere-zero vanishing
contents.support: The library's AT page supplies the definition and properties; DT-12 cites them without redefinition.

contents.name: Theorem 138/139: the Poincare dual of an embedded submanifold is the Thom class of its normal bundle
contents.support: Proved here in the tubular-neighbourhood form with the library's cap conventions, including the sign normalization the notes leave implicit.

contents.name: The intersection product diagram: [P].[Q] is Poincare dual to PD[P] cup PD[Q]
contents.support: The central AT interface, proved through the normal-bundle restriction computation.

contents.name: Corollary 143: degree of a map as the sum of local signs
contents.support: The evaluation of the zero-dimensional class on the fundamental class is the local signed sum consumed in the theorem's proof.

contents.name: Theorem 144 and its proof: self-intersection and the Euler class of the normal bundle
contents.support: The main geometric statement, with the transverse-section zero count made precise.

contents.name: Examples 145-146: complex projective lines and Chern classes of tautological bundles
contents.reason: The complex projective and Chern-class computations belong to the Chern/Pontryagin pages of the algebraic-topology track and involve no differential-topology intersection result of this pair; nothing on this page cites them.

sources.locator: Sections 9-12, printed pp. 95-146: Section 9 Oriented Bundles and the Euler Class; Section 10 The Thom Isomorphism Theorem; Section 11 Computations in a Smooth Manifold; Section 12 Obstructions.
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 326-page PDF (13,204,109 bytes) and located the table of contents and the section starts of Sections 9-12 with the text layer (the OCR layer is noisy, so the exact statements used here were additionally verified against Cohen Theorem 9.9/Corollary 9.3 and Ionel Theorems 139/144, which prove the same identities). Section 11 is the dual-class intersection calculus; Section 12 contains the obstruction-theoretic companion of the nowhere-zero criterion.

contents.name: Section 9: the Euler class of an oriented bundle, naturality, products and orientation sign
contents.support: The library's AT page proves these properties; DT-12 consumes them.

contents.name: Section 10: the Thom isomorphism theorem
contents.support: Consumed through the AT Thom interface.

contents.name: Section 11: computations in a smooth manifold -- dual classes and intersection numbers
contents.support: Independent classical treatment backing the dual-class intersection calculus; the ordered factor signs are reconciled with the library conventions in this page's proof.

contents.name: Section 12: obstructions and the Euler class of a bundle with a section
contents.support: The class-level vanishing criterion; this page adds its geometric numerical consequences.
